law_name: State Budget for 2025 (Lei do Orçamento do Estado para 2025)
description: First budget of the Montenegro government, approved in the final vote on 29 November 2024 with PSD and CDS-PP in favour and the PS abstaining; Chega, IL, PAN, Livre, PCP and BE voted against. It carried the reformulated IRS Jovem (an income-tax exemption for workers up to 35 for up to 10 years, in decreasing bands, capped at 55 times the IAS index) and a one-point cut in corporate tax to 20%.
significance: Passed by a minority government thanks to the abstention of the main opposition party, after negotiations that changed both flagship tax measures.

law_name: Government decree exempting young buyers' first homes from IMT, stamp duty and fees, and public guarantee for their mortgages
description: Decree-law promulgated by the President in July 2024 and applied from 1 August 2024: buyers up to 35 pay no property transfer tax (IMT), stamp duty or registration fees on a first permanent home up to €316,772, with partial exemption up to €633,453; a separate scheme gives a state guarantee of up to 15% of the purchase price. The 2027 budget proposal raises the full-exemption ceiling to about €338,000.
significance: One of the government's main housing measures for young people.

law_name: Recovery of teachers' frozen service time (6 years, 6 months and 23 days)
description: Regime agreed with several teachers' unions in May 2024 and enacted by the government, returning the frozen career time in four 25% tranches, the first in September 2024 and the last on 1 July 2027.
significance: Addresses the long-running dispute with teachers over frozen career time; the final tranche is funded in the 2027 budget proposal.

law_name: Repeal of the 'manifestação de interesse' residence route (Migration Action Plan)
description: Announced on 3 June 2024 as part of the government's migration plan: foreigners can no longer enter Portugal (for example on a tourist visa) and then apply for a residence permit through an expression of interest; they must apply from abroad with a work or other visa.
significance: First step in tightening immigration policy, presented by Montenegro as a response to 'excessive abuse' of the system.

law_name: Council of Ministers decision on the location of the new Lisbon airport (Aeroporto Luís de Camões, Alcochete)
description: On 14 May 2024 the government chose the Alcochete shooting range (Campo de Tiro de Alcochete) for the new Lisbon airport, following the independent technical commission, to replace Humberto Delgado airport entirely; in February 2026 it imposed preventive land-use measures over about 71,000 hectares around the site.
significance: Montenegro presented it as resolving an 'impasse of decades'; construction by the concessionaire ANA has not yet started.

law_name: Amendment to the Corporate Income Tax Code reducing the general IRC rate to 17% by 2028
description: Government bill cutting the general corporate tax rate by one point a year, from 20% to 19% in 2026, 18% in 2027 and 17% in 2028, and the rate on the first €50,000 of profit of small and mid-sized companies from 16% to 15%. Approved in principle on 19 September 2025 and in the final vote on 17 October 2025 with PSD, CDS-PP, Chega, IL, PAN and JPP; promulgated on 3 November 2025.
significance: Delivers part of the promised cut to 15%; passed with Chega's votes, at an estimated cost of about €300 million a year per point.

law_name: Amendment to the Foreigners Act (Lei n.º 23/2007, regime of entry, stay, exit and removal of foreigners)
description: Approved by the first Council of Ministers of the XXV Government and passed by parliament with Chega's votes; after the Constitutional Court found five provisions of the first version unconstitutional, a revised text approved on 30 September 2025 by about 70% of MPs was promulgated on 16 October 2025. Among other changes, it lengthens the time an immigrant must wait before applying for family reunification.
significance: Central plank of the government's policy of reducing immigration flows.

law_name: State Budget for 2026 (Lei do Orçamento do Estado para 2026)
description: Approved in the final vote on 27 November 2025 with PSD and CDS-PP in favour and the PS abstaining; Chega, IL, Livre, PCP, BE, PAN and JPP voted against. PS leader José Luís Carneiro said the abstention avoided a new political crisis.
significance: Second budget passed by the AD minority with PS abstention.

law_name: Amendment to the Nationality Law (Lei da Nacionalidade)
description: Raises the legal-residence requirement for naturalisation from five to at least seven years for citizens of Portuguese-speaking countries and to at least ten years for other foreigners; pending applications keep the previous rules. After the Constitutional Court found parts of the first decree unconstitutional, a second version was approved on 1 April 2026 by PSD, Chega, IL and CDS-PP, with PS, Livre, PCP, BE and PAN against and JPP abstaining, promulgated by President António José Seguro on 3 May 2026 with criticism of the lack of broader consensus, and in force from 19 May 2026.
significance: Second major immigration-related law of the XXV Government passed with Chega's votes; a separate decree creating loss of nationality as an accessory criminal penalty was approved on 13 April 2026 (RTP).

law_name: Decree-law raising the guaranteed minimum monthly wage to €920 from 1 January 2026
description: Published on 29 December 2025 in execution of the 2025–2028 agreement signed in October 2024 with the employers' confederations and the UGT: a 5.7% rise from €870.
significance: Step towards the programme target of €1,100 in 2029.

law_name: Privatisation of TAP Air Portugal: sale of 49.9% to Lufthansa
description: On 14 October 2026 the Council of Ministers approved the privatisation of 49.9% of TAP (44.9% to an industrial partner plus a 5% offer to employees at the same price) to Lufthansa, for €1,201 million including the employees' tranche and the sale of two subsidiaries, over Air France-KLM's €1,038 million. Lufthansa also proposed a second phase for the remaining 50.1%, which Montenegro wants to complete by 2028.
significance: Lufthansa becomes TAP's industrial partner, with commitments to enlarge the fleet; a second phase for full privatisation would need parliamentary support from PS or Chega.
